free_tier.stated: Free access to MET Norway's archive of historical weather and climate observations (quality controlled daily, monthly and yearly measurements of temperature, precipitation and wind, and station metadata) with a client ID issued for an email address; no numeric request quota is published.
free_tier.notes: Heavy traffic is defined as more than 1 request a second on average, which should be cached locally; users with high load or bad traffic patterns can be blocked. Large requests time out and are split by station or by time range. Bulk path: none beyond split requests; gridded model data are on THREDDS (see data-apis/met-norway).

per_object_cap.stated: requests that are too large time out; the vendor advises splitting, for example 1000 stations into 10 requests of 100

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at frost.met.no with Basic authentication (client ID as user name, empty password) or OAuth2; JSON-LD answers
tooling: any HTTP client; examples for curl, Python and Java are published
chaining: The historical-observation companion to the keyless api.met.no forecasts: station data by source, reference time and element.

limits.value: more than 1 request a second on average is heavy traffic that should be cached; no hard number is published
requests that are too large answer a timeout and must be split

binding_note: Only the 1 request a second guideline is stated, so the sustained rate binds first.

identity_cost.detail: A client ID and secret are issued after registering with an email address; each client ID must be tied to a valid email address. The form's other fields were not readable.

reliability_note: No delivery guarantee; clients with high load or bad traffic patterns can be blocked.
confidence_note: Identity and traffic rules are read from first-party pages; a call with no client ID answered HTTP 401, so a keyed call was not exercised.

evidence.proved: Frost serves MET Norway's historical observation archive
evidence.quote: This data includes quality controlled daily, monthly, and yearly measurements of temperature, precipitation, and wind data.

evidence.proved: an email address gives a client ID
evidence.quote: To gain access to the Frost API services, register with your email address to generate a new client ID and client secret.

evidence.proved: every data request needs a client ID
evidence.quote: Requests for data (typically everything else than static HTML-pages) must be authenticated with a client ID

evidence.proved: more than 1 request a second on average counts as heavy traffic, to be cached locally
evidence.quote: Heavy traffic means on average more than 1 requests to the API per second.

evidence.proved: a client ID needs a valid email address; several IDs per address are allowed
evidence.quote: Each client ID must be associated with a valid email address. It is possible to register multiple client IDs for each email address.

evidence.proved: large requests time out and must be split
evidence.quote: If your request is too large, you will get a timeout error.
There are no guarantees of delivery regarding this service.

notes: Observations only; forecasts are on api.met.no.
